author: althoufx
text:
i mean most of the times i place a long or short, price stops
immediately any move it was doing (even trend, rally or drop) then
starts to CP against my entry.

It seems a Stop Loss hunting, but against one order ?! ....i can't really think it is like this !

Sometimes it CPs for minutes (half an hour), other times it takes
hours, then the price turns to the direction i wanted (if the trade was
good...) and my trade goes from minus to plus and starts to make profit.

...but the reaction against is real, almost always !! it seems the price reacts to one order !

I know if it was always like this, the trades with minimal SL ( the extremes by IF ) would not be possible...so i'm wrong for sure, ...specially my entries i think...

....but it's really impressive how much often it happens, also for good trades !

did you notice something like this ?

all the best

Yes that was my impression too when I started to trade with candle
price action, I saw a nice pin bar rejecting a key level and once I

what the ITs need to do to create the liquidity to fill their orders.

author: Jurij
text:
althoufx , good call.

When price respects an important S/R it is a good continuation signal,
whereas the engulf signals intention to reverse price (obvious )

That was surely an S/R but price really reacted to a flag limit.

If price rejects an S/R but engulfs its flag limit then you better stay aside from such trade.

You wrote: too simple and evident, well think about it this way: the ITs
 must sometimes respect S/R levels, pivots, moving averages, gartleys,
fibs and so on..., to give the false hope of a working system with an
edge to the many technical traders out there.

Those provide the liquidity once the ITs deploy our loved signal
(engulf) and then prepare one or multiple ad hoc technical traps.

Check out this excellent
 post
.

author: Bodostock
text:
Hi Juril

Am i right that yours was a QM trade?

But was yours a touch-trade or PA trade? It seemed to me it was a touch-trade.

I was actually looking at this pair too.

However, i was awaiting for PA to enter in M15 but couldn't convince myself to take the trade.

Hope you can guide me on this.

There was at first i thought a M15 QM formed. But it formed right below
the H4 supply zone and not inside it ( the one you marked), so i was
skeptical it will work when price bounced back to the QM level,
especially when the LL did not engulf the last FL or pole base.

So okay, price bounced back and somehow did react to the QM level, but
my intent was to see a bigger reaction of price coming down as per where
 it is now.

So price reached back to near the last M15 LL and began to compress up
which i was expecting this. It then had a CP-lq into the H4 supply
zone.

Price flagged and broke down ( Pro-sellers selling at the top?)

Then as it reached the pole base, it bounced back up to the flag. Would you consider that as a can can?

I was hoping that price engulfed the M15 pole base and i would have take entry when price reached the flag.

But because it did not engulf, i was not confident to take the trade. So ended up, i failed to enter at the top.

Okay, now, price then fell hard, not only went back to the previous M15 LL, it engulfed into the next PAZ.

I was then lost, not knowing how to find the next best trade to ride along this fall.

Now I decided to let price find its target first and then wait for the next opportunity to short.

Thank you

Hi Jurij

your trade on EURUSD i think has really a lot of meaning. I'm following
specially that wide CP because it is dense of actions, creating PAZs
evident and so on...

You used both the most significant moves the price makes to show the
intentions: ENG and FO (... the points i'm focusing on right now )

I think ENG and FO, since they have different functions and give
opposite information, should have a logical coordination, so the one as
first and the other as second with a precise meaning.

ITs want liquid money (SL) so first they take orders, and after they take respective SL

When there are 2 moves, like in your trade, the first must be always ENG
 (where the price will go to), so the second always FO (where the price
will escape from), as you got correctly in your trade , i think opposite should not be possible...

....by the truth i think ITs take every orders (SELL and BUY all
together, then respective SL when price goes opposite) but however FO
should be always the last spike (...the second)....so what to say about
the same chart, a bit later ?

any comments precious as usually

many thanks Jurij

author: althoufx
text:
hello Jurij and everybody

more on this USDCAD, because things like that happens so often ! ......
thinks and opinions...but it's important to compare if we want to
discover the mistakes , hope you agree it

RTM makes clear one thing as first : the Price says always where it goes to. As far me personally i'm more and more believing this is strongly true.

Why Price does it, i can't say yet, but since it does it, it is aimed to
 somebody reading it somewhere !! So we assume it can be readed...

Price uses basic signals in different combinations....like any language, i think.

So in order to read, we must learn that language. To uncover the
signals, we build instruments that do not exist in the real market, like
 the boxes for example.

The boxes have meaning if they are built by fixed rules, so they must be
 standard. Boxes are used to compare levels (i think) and to reveal our
loved engulfs

so the Boxes :

...have top in a Swing Higher High and bottom in the Swing Low
immediately subsequent in case of rally. Obviously Boxes depend onTime
Frame

...have bottom in a Swing Lower Low and top in the Swing High
immediately subsequent in case of drop. Obviously Boxes depend on Time
Frame

then it is very important how we build our boxes...even difficult for
LLTF ...as more noisy Time Frames are, as more difficult box drawing is

...but what else could we do.....maybe to read only HTF can be a good method

in that USDCAD i think the boxes built by these rules only gave LTF bullish signals

..i'd really like some words from upside in the ladder ...but i'm afraid there won't be anymore that time...

many thanks, all the best
